$comment: Canonical status source for the unpingable site. Edit here, then run tools/render_status.py. Current rows describe public releases; historical rows remain explicitly marked as history.
generated_note: Rendered into constellation/status.html by tools/render_status.py. Do not hand-edit the ledger block.

objects.name: Constellation 0.1.0-alpha.6 — reviewed local copy
objects.claim: One exact local-copy plan was independently reviewed, explicitly accepted, authorized once, executed under Docket custody, settled successfully, and followed by a read-only observation. An anonymous public-clone reproduction verified the retained evidence without repeating the provider call or effect.
objects.verified_by: the immutable alpha.6 manifest, qualification record, walkthrough, and anonymous public-clone verification
objects.promotion: This release is immutable. Operational burn-in, live notification delivery, cross-version restore, migration, rollback, and production consumer adoption require separate evidence.

objects.name: reviewed-local-copy/v1 — Alpha 2 release candidate, clean install
objects.claim: Packaged builds of NQ, Maude, Nightshift, Pulse, AG, Docket, Switchyard and the App Server, with a setup kit, were installed into a fresh Debian 12 virtual machine from those artifacts alone. One reviewed and accepted occurrence settled successfully and wrote its file exactly once. Every requested refusal held: a wrong artifact digest, a repeated init, a stale review, an expired authorization, a second execution attempt, and acceptance of the wrong candidate. The review came from a local fixture standing in for the model provider, and the acceptance was performed by the test harness, not by a person.
objects.verified_by: clean-install run-004 on 2026-09-25: 31 pass, 0 fail, 0 not exercised, with setup kit 0.4.0. It reruns every earlier case, including a check that the evidence verifier shipped in the kit gives the same result inside the virtual machine as outside it and a replay of the settled evidence without the issuer's private key, and adds cases from the hostile review: the review's altered setup kits and substitute artifact were run against the new bundle and refused, and an already-installed NQ is now compared with the package file by file. An earlier upgrade-continuity run (run-002: 22 pass, 0 fail, 0 not exercised) upgraded an install of the previous kit to a second, test-only build and re-verified the first build's retained evidence, byte for byte; the upgrade code is unchanged in kit 0.4.0, so it was not rerun. Both run records are retained privately; the harness source is public on an unmerged branch.

evidence.label: the released alpha.6 profile it packages

objects.promotion: This is not a release. The packaged artifacts are not public. Alpha 1 proved the semantics; Alpha 2 claims only that the same composition can be packaged, installed, reproduced and upgraded as one set of versions outside the development environment; Beta, an operator experience someone can actually live in, is not claimed. The candidate awaits the operator's own acceptance run against the real model provider, and its packaging branches stay unmerged until then. A clean-room newcomer run succeeded on 2026-09-25. A hostile review the same day found that an altered setup kit passed the kit pin check; that is fixed and the attack was refused in run-004. It also found that whoever controls the operator's host account can run the packaged executor directly, without an AG issuance or Docket custody. That is not fixed: it is documented as the local trust boundary and needs component changes. The paid review route also sends one non-generating warm-up request whose billing is unverified. Both are open items for a beta. Nothing is released beyond 0.1.0-alpha.6 and the NQ 0.2.0 component package.

objects.name: Indeterminate-effect demo (refund with a lost reply)
objects.status: cold-clone qualified; tagged public exhibit, not a Docket release
objects.claim: An agent reports a refund done after the reply was lost. Docket, built from source, records the attempt as indeterminate, sends nothing twice, and settles success or failure only on a separate observer's read of the provider's ledger. A second run with the request lost ends in failure under the same agent claim. Docket is real; the authorization signer (a stand-in reproducing AG's published test vector), the payment provider, the faulty network link and the agent are local stand-ins. Everything runs on one host under one clock.
objects.verified_by: run-003: an anonymous HTTPS clone of the demo source into a fresh Debian 12 virtual machine, with the network cut off for the build and the run; the demo exited 0 and its independent check passed 53 of 53 checks. The exhibit tag demo/indeterminate-effect-20260925 (eeb0534) carries the same demo code; only the README changed.
objects.promotion: The tag is a qualified public exhibit, not a Docket release or cohort promotion; the demo counts as part of Docket only once it is merged there. Independence holds because this demo's worker delegates reconcile to the observer; Docket does not pin that configuration, so it is not a general guarantee. Using AG itself, a remote provider, or several observers would each need separate evidence.

objects.name: Constellation Docket
objects.claim: Takes custody of one authorized attempt, dispatches an authority-neutral executor, and records settlement and reconciliation. Alpha.6 exercised its bounded local permission snapshot and local-copy executor path.
objects.verified_by: the alpha.6 manifest and qualification record at the exact pinned public revision
objects.promotion: The profile is narrow; it does not establish production hardening or arbitrary executor compatibility.

objects.name: Constellation AG
objects.claim: Checks whether exact automated work is admissible and grants bounded one-use authority for one specific run. It does not execute work or infer permission from a provider response.
objects.verified_by: the alpha.6 one-use authorization and public evidence-reader checks
objects.promotion: No family-wide or production maturity is claimed.

objects.name: Constellation NQ
objects.claim: Evaluates retained evidence under named profiles and keeps missing, stale, unavailable, or uncertain results visible. Its results do not authorize an effect.
objects.verified_by: alpha.2 through alpha.6 profiles and the separately documented archive-read procedure
objects.promotion: Live Slack or Discord delivery, cross-version restore, production migration, and rollback remain unqualified.

objects.name: Constellation NQ 0.2.0 component package
objects.claim: A Debian package and a tarball for NQ alone, built twice offline with identical bytes and accepted in a clean Debian 12 virtual machine (49 pass, 0 fail, 2 not exercised). It packages one component; it is not an installable Constellation suite.
objects.verified_by: the published GitHub release, whose assets were downloaded and checked against their recorded digests and the qualified copies
objects.promotion: NQ's maturity stays developer preview. The package does not qualify any other component or composition.
